intended_object: The standard graph embedding of the path graph P₂ (a single edge 0–1) into the path graph Pₙ for n ≥ 2, sending vertices 0 and 1 to the first two vertices of Pₙ. Inferred from the docstring and name.
explanation:
I found no existing Mathlib definition of this embedding: the search turned up only this one and some unrelated embeddings of `(pathGraph 3)ᶜ`.

The map sends `v : Fin 2` to `⟨v, _⟩ : Fin n`. This is the inclusion of {0, 1} into {0, …, n−1}, i.e. `Fin.castLE h`. It is injective because `Fin.mk` is injective on values.

The embedding condition (`map_rel_iff'`) also holds. In `pathGraph k`, two vertices are adjacent exactly when their values differ by 1, because `pathGraph` is defined as the Hasse diagram of `Fin k`. The map does not change values, so adjacency holds in P₂ exactly when it holds between the images in Pₙ.

The hypothesis `2 ≤ n` is exactly what is needed for the target to have two vertices. So the definition is a correct statement of the specific embedding described in the docstring.

One could write a more general `pathGraph m ↪g pathGraph n` for `m ≤ n`. However, this is a specific, concrete map, used locally in the coloring constructions. It is not a general notion stated in an unnecessarily special type-theoretic setting, so I do not count it as too narrow.
